title: Acquire a friend (Avot 1:6)
hookLine: friendship is something you make, even pay for
tomorrow: a tent with a way in on every side. whose, and why?

lines: MAKE A TEACHER, ACQUIRE A FRIEND.
cards: Grown-up friendship runs on calendars: weeks of 'we should get coffee' before anyone actually does.

A sage in Pirkei Avot, Yehoshua ben Perachiah, gives advice that sounds almost like shopping: make for yourself a teacher, and acquire for yourself a friend. Acquire, like buying. Can a friend be bought?
Inside the tradition, there are two answers.

teach.h: ACQUIRE, NOT MAKE: EVEN AT A COST.
teach.b: View one: yes, in a way, because friendship takes spending. Maimonides, commenting on this line, points out that it says acquire, not make, and reads it this way: get a friend even if it costs you.
And an old companion to Avot, Avot de-Rabbi Natan, spells out what acquiring looks like: eat with your friend, drink with them, study with them, trust them with your secrets.
The best case for this view: friendships nobody invests in quietly fade, and the people who keep friends are the ones who actually plan the coffee. View two is also in Avot.
Love that depends on something ends when the something ends.
Love that depends on nothing never ends. Its example is David and Jonathan.
The best case for this view: a friendship you've 'acquired' by effort can start to feel like a deal, and the deepest friendships aren't calculated. Put them side by side and they stop fighting.
The first view is about how a friendship starts and lasts: time, food and honesty, spent on purpose. The second is about what it's for: nothing but the friend.

teach.h: SPEND ON THEM, NOT FOR SOMETHING.
teach.b: You spend on a friend, not to get something back.
Something to tell a friend tonight: Maimonides read acquire a friend as permission to spend money on one.

how: Jewish study can happen in pairs, chavruta, where two learners become study partners and sometimes close friends; some communities read Pirkei Avot on summer Shabbat afternoons, chapter by chapter.

o: to wait for a friendship that happens by luck
to make a friendship on purpose, even at a cost
to find a study teacher who will train you

games.q: two views of friendship — tap the pairs.

s: Pirkei Avot says real friendship shouldn't take effort
Avot 1:6 says acquire a friend; Maimonides: even at a cost.
Avot names David and Jonathan as love that depends on nothing
that love, it says, never ends.
acquire a friend means paying people to like you
the commentaries mean time, food, study and trust, spent on purpose.

games.q: your friend says scheduling friends feels fake: real friendship should just happen. you like planning. what's her side's best case, from Avot?
o: love that depends on nothing never ends; the deepest friendships aren't a deal.
friends should never spend money or time on each other.
Avot says friends are found by luck, never made.
games.why: that's Avot 5:16, David and Jonathan. your side has its best case too: Avot 1:6, acquire a friend, even at a cost.

practice: Open a message to one friend you've let drift. Write the first move of acquiring: an actual plan, with a day, a place and something to eat. Not 'we should hang out.' Whether you send it now or later, the plan is the spending.

wordCard.voice: Acquire a friend: from Avot. Friendship you make on purpose, with time, food and honesty, even when it costs.

orig.note: Hebrew: acquire for yourself a friend (Avot 1:6).

carryVoice: Hold onto this: make a friend, and spend on them for nothing in return. Day eleven, invested.
